how: A member proposes a character and starts its right eye before another participant reports joining the work.
A builder recruits help because working alone has become difficult, and later participants renew requests for helpers.
Character proposals become practical design instructions specifying the head, hat, eyes, and skin.
Public update posts report progress and later what remains, without their titles independently establishing the linked images' contents.
Requests for a location receive anchor coordinates, while linked guides and part dimensions make joining practical.
A newcomer asks what the canvas is and receives an explanation of its one-pixel placement rule.
A defender explicitly judges personal effort insufficient and asks others to help preserve the drawing.
Joining can first require an explanation of the event, confirmation that it is still active, and directions to the drawing.
Calls may recruit into already begun work, so later progress reports do not establish that recruitment initiated building.
Starting the right eye gives others a concrete project to join, with proposal, existing work, and recruitment compressed into the same turn.
An update elicits defense talk, but the respondent reports hours of prior defense, so posting the update cannot be treated as starting upkeep.
Guides settle action only among those adopting the same start, since an already working group explicitly declines an invitation to consolidate.
Voluntary continuation and task instructions do not establish the absence of decided order throughout the room or test the claim's cross-room frequency.
The repair report describes repeated effort without identifying scripts, spare accounts, or any placement method.
A bare statement of joining the defense receives a bare thank-you without requesting anything further.
A defense plea receives an existing defender's report, a bare joining response, and thanks, supporting a local acceptance sequence rather than a universal obligation.
The reasoned refusal rejects merging projects while continuing canvas participation, so refusal must be specified by the particular proposal being declined.
Participants recruit defenders, report repairing altered colours and eyes, and commit to joining another defender.
Upkeep describes particular participants' commitments rather than a shared room norm when another speaker treats continual interference as the event's purpose.
A participant explains interference as predictable interest in changing a longstanding drawing, without identifying particular placers or communities.
A fairness dispute cannot automatically count as restraint when its speaker endorses interference instead of asking anyone to spare a drawing.
Treat accepting continual alteration as the canvas's purpose as a distinct position, since restraint and attribution alone do not capture its disagreement with preservation.
A participant offers help preserving the drawing after finishing work in another community, without claiming a reciprocal arrangement.
Outside help may arrive through a volunteer who has finished another drawing, without the recipient making a recorded inter-room request or bargain.
Separate an alliance proposal and an individual's offered backing from subsequent acceptance, coalition membership, and joint defense.
A statement that communities could form an alliance establishes an attempt only, unless acceptance or coordinated membership is evidenced.
The surviving proposal and backing do not resolve whether an alliance formed because the initiating body and subsequent reply are deleted.
Defense precedes an alliance suggestion, but no passage connects them causally or establishes that the proposed coalition acted together.
A greeting and proposed alliance do not establish a negotiated border or truce, while deleted initiating and response material prevents resolving a possible agreement.
A surviving greeting and supportive reply cannot establish whether anyone was authorized to carry a room's proposal between venues.
Adding a blue border for assimilation and fitting a smaller face among drawings do not establish a host's permission or rule over guests.
One participant reports the original overwritten and claims a smaller face made elsewhere among neighbouring drawings.
The smaller remake supports individual rebuilding, while collective deliberation, weighing another fight against moving, and continuity with the initial starts remain unresolved.
A shortage plea and a later maker's account supply no passage attributing relocation to insufficient hands or a decision to stop fighting.
The surviving alliance proposal and backing contain no dispute about who may commit a community to an agreement.
A proposed alliance with missing initiating and response material cannot test whether a settled agreement prompted disputes over representative authority.
Defense and a later alliance proposal do not show that upkeep brought the room into border negotiations with the people changing its pixels.
No settled border is recoverable, and the comment accepting alteration cannot supply the predicted restraint after such an agreement.
An outside volunteer and a later alliance proposal do not show border talks opening a channel for an exchange of help.
Fandom language supplies a defense demand through AUTHORITAH and a wall joke answering the explanation of interference.
The wall joke supplies fandom language without establishing an actual quarrel carried into the canvas from before the event.
The wall joke identifies no evidenced rival or attack action, so it cannot test whether a prior tie names a target in an attack turn.
A vote threshold proposes a subreddit takeover that participants perform through mock trailers, alternatives, celebration, and criticism.
The takeover's vote threshold and moderator demand concern the host joke, so they cannot establish a canvas vote or insincerity of independent drawing calls.
Calling on moderators to enact a host joke supplies no observed boundary governing canvas posts or response to a canvas flood.
Canvas recruitment and the separate moderator demand do not show calls causing a posting flood or a rule containing it.
A starter explicitly credits a named helper for work on the blue border.
Credit occurs during unfinished work and in an individual's loss-and-remake report, so completion of a shared mark cannot be required as its trigger.
The maker records the original's replacement and describes the smaller face's position among neighbouring drawings before placement ends.
Credit and fate reports are visible, but no passage establishes that marking the work together prompted recording its history.
A smaller face on the same active canvas supplies no decision about a successor canvas, emblem adoption, or lasting collective.
Reporting the lost original does not show a later decision to carry the temporary effort into another purpose.
The post-close coded exchange concerns using Reddit and supplies no dispute over cleaned images or which canvas history should survive.
A defender reports damage and another speaker accepts alteration, but neither concept shows the room calling or carrying out an attack.
The wall joke cannot establish talk directed against an evidenced rival community.
The surviving calls recruit building and defense rather than documenting recruitment turning into an attack call.
Without an observed attack call by this room, disagreement about preserving drawings cannot test the predicted reasoned refusal of an attack.
The alliance proposal names no prior attack call or truce, leaving the predicted attack-to-negotiation mechanism untestable.
A wall joke without an evidenced attack call or rival exchange cannot test whether attack turns into an inter-room contest in talk.
Defense strain is explicit, but a turn toward scripts or spare accounts is not observed.
Retain ordinary conversation inside the event thread as local residue without assigning the question and answer an evidenced canvas function.
